fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Vegetation Near Structure; Patio Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so arriving units do not lose time identifying the access point.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so responding units can pull to the structure without obstruction.
• Designate a parking area away from the access drive so responding units have a clear staging area that does not block the drive.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive that narrows the travel width or reduces overhead clearance for responding vehicles.
• Cut back vegetation growing against or directly adjacent to both the main residence and the detached structure to create a clear buffer around each building.
• Mark any walking path from the front of the property to the rear so responders can quickly locate a route between the two structures.
• Install a gate, or keep any existing gate unlocked and clearly marked, on any fenced boundary that limits movement to the rear of the property.
• Post a simple site diagram at the driveway entrance or front door showing the location of the detached structure, rear access route, and utility shutoffs so responding units can orient quickly on arrival.
• Identify and mark the utility shutoff locations on the exterior of both structures so responders can locate them without entering.

wildfire.conditions: Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation; Open Green Space; Grass Cover; Vegetation Along Driveway; Single Access Route; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches and shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the house on any side.
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to create open spacing between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing beneath or between scattered trees close to the house to reduce connected burning paths from the yard to the structure.
• Cut grass areas near the house and outbuildings short and keep them mowed regularly.
• Trim overhanging tree branches along the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Clear shrubs and low branches along the driveway edges to keep the travel path open and visible.
• Remove any dead wood, fallen branches, or dry plant material from the ground around the structure.
• Thin shrubs in mixed vegetation areas close to the house so plants are not touching or overlapping each other.
• Keep the single driveway access route clear of debris and overgrowth at all times to allow emergency vehicles to reach the structure.
• Separate shrub groupings near the house so there is open bare ground or short grass between them and the building.
